content.text: BAMS is a 5.5-year undergraduate course that offers hands-on experience in the field of Ayurveda. A lot of colleges are extending their boundaries to make this course available to students all over India. Just like all over the country, BAMS in Haryana is also flourishing. There are a total of 15 colleges that offer the Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery in Haryana. sections.heading: BAMS Admission in Haryana Overview

content.text: The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) is mandatory for admission in BAMS program. Students who are willing to pursue BAMS must qualify for the NEET after their 12th board exam and then attend the Haryana AYUSH counselling session to get BAMS admission in Haryana. The counselling authority that conducts the state AYUSH counselling is Shri Krishna Ayush University, Kurukshetra . A total of 1053 BAMS seats are available there, out of which 213 are government seats, and the rest 840 are private seats. 4 Government Institutions and 11 private ones take up admission for BAMS each year. So, there are a lot of opportunities for students who are willing to take BAMS admission in Haryana.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Haryana

content.text: For the students who want to take BAMS admission in Haryana, there are some steps that must be followed chronologically, which is given below.
Step 1: Candidates must apply for NEET UG on the official website of the National Testing Agency (NTA). Then, they need to appear in the examination and score a minimum percentile.

Step 2: When the NEET results are declared, qualified students have to register for Haryana AYUSH Counselling from the official website at https://skau.ac.in/. The registration fee for the Unreserved category is INR 2000/-, and INR 500/- for the Reserved category.
Step 3: Attend the counselling session online, and make your choice of colleges according to your preferences.
Step 4: Depending on the student’s NEET UG Rank and choice filling, a student shall be allotted to a college for BAMS admission.
Step 5: The next step requires the students to report to the allotted college. Carry the necessary documents, both in originals and photocopies, and complete the document verification there.
Step 6: After completion of document verification, the final step is to confirm one’s seat allotment to the college. Here, the applicants need to pay the prescribed course fees to confirm their seat.

There are a total of 4 counselling rounds in Haryana’s BAMS admission process – Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and Stray Vacancy Round. If a candidate is not allotted to a college in the first round, he/she must wait for the next round of counselling.

sections.heading: BAMS Eligibility Criteria in Haryana

content.text: A set of eligibility criteria is there for BAMS admission in Haryana, including academic qualification, age requirement, and entrance exams. They are described in detail below.

items: Candidates must pass their 12th examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB subjects) from a recognized board.
They must secure at least 50% or above aggregate in the PCB subjects. (40% for the reserved candidates, and 45% for PwD candidates)
Appear and qualify for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG), conducted by NTA and score above the cut-off mark, set by the couselling authority of Haryana.
Students must have a minimum age of 17 years as of December 31st of the admission year.

sections.heading: Documents Required for BAMS Admission in Haryana

content.text: The Haryana AYUSH counselling authority has published a list of documents that are required for BAMS admission in Haryana. The following list consists of those documents. They are required to be submitted at the time of document verification, both in originals and photocopies. Failing to produce the original documents will result in the cancellation of the candidature.

items: NEET-UG 2025 Admit & Score Card
Matriculation/High School Certificate (10th)
10+2/Intermediate/Senior Secondary School Examination Certificate & Detailed Marks Sheet.
Character Certificate issued by the school/institute last attended.
Resident Certificate (if applicable)
Certificate of bona fide resident issued by the competent authority(if applicable)
Caste Certificate issued by a competent authority (if applicable)
Latest Income Certificate (if applicable)
PwD Certificate (If applicable)
Certificate of Dependent of Freedom Fighters issued by the competent authority (if applicable).
Print out of Online Application form.
Provisional Allotment letter.
Proof of identification: Aadhaar card/PAN Card/Driving license/Passport/Voter ID/Ration Card/any other (any two).
Four passport-size photographs against a white background (preferably the photograph used in the NEET form).

content.text: In total, there are currently 15 colleges that are offering the BAMS admission in Haryana. Both Government and Private colleges provide this course. With the best infrastructure and well-trained faculty, they promise to make education available to the students to become professional Ayurvedic personnel. Although seat availability is different in the government and private colleges, each has its own set of advantages.

sections.heading: BAMS Course Fees in Haryana

content.text: The BAMS course fees in Haryana are different depending on the type of institute you are choosing. As the Ministry of AYUSH and the Government of India have jointly agreed to give the colleges freedom in selecting their fee structure, the course fees are different in every college. Government colleges have lower course fees, while private ones promise the best infrastructure and faculty with competitive fees.

BAMS Careers in Haryana

content.text: There is a path of diverse career options for BAMS graduates in Haryana. They can find work as Ayurvedic practitioners in clinics or hospitals, pursue research, teach in Ayurvedic institutions, or explore opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry, wellness tourism, and more. BAMS jobs in Haryana aren’t only available in the private sector. There are BAMS govt jobs in Haryana, including positions like Medical Officer (BAMS), Resident Medical Officer (RMO), and Ayurvedic Doctor in various hospitals and healthcare facilities. Students who want to pursue higher studies have many options to choose from, including many Ayurved PG courses.
